intro: A threshold must move an entire tied-score group at once. Build operating points from unique scores so the reported precision and recall correspond to actual decisions.
task: Build achievable precision-recall operating points, moving every tied-score group together as the threshold changes.
requirements: labels is a nonempty binary integer-valued vector and scores is a same-length finite real vector. At least one label must be positive.
At each unique score in descending order, predict positive for scores >= threshold. Return arrays thresholds, precision, and recall at those points.
Do not add artificial endpoints or interpolate. Scores are ranking values, not necessarily probabilities, and ties must enter together.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Group by distinct score
hints.body: A deployment threshold cannot split observations with identical scores.

hints.title: Recall has a fixed denominator
hints.body: Divide every true-positive count by the total number of positive labels.

explanation: The curve is a sequence of achievable decision rules. Moving tied observations one at a time would invent operating points that no threshold can reproduce.
This lesson reports observed points without integrating an area. Average precision and trapezoidal PR area make different aggregation choices and should not be silently substituted.
